AuthZENAccessEvaluationItem.description:
One item in an AuthZEN 1.0 boxcar request. The top-level request supplies
defaults for omitted fields, as defined by Section 7.1 of the standard.

additionalProperties.description:
AuthZEN extensions are accepted without changing the core decision
model. Reserved authentication-context names are retained so the HTTP
boundary can reject an attempted trust override instead of silently
discarding it.

AuthZENAccessEvaluationRequest.description:
AuthZEN 1.0 Access Evaluation request.

Authentication and trusted identity context are deliberately not part of
this wire type. The route derives them from the authenticated PEP
credential and, for bearer credentials, from an independently verified
JWT.

AuthZENAccessEvaluationsRequest.description:
AuthZEN 1.0 Access Evaluations request. Unknown fields are intentionally
ignored so standards extensions do not change the core adapter contract.

AuthZENAccessEvaluationsResponse.description:
Response envelope for `/access/v1/evaluations`.

The envelope is returned even when the request omits `evaluations` or sends
an empty array and relies on top-level defaults. That request form resolves
to one effective evaluation, while the batch endpoint keeps its generated
response shape.

AuthZENAction.description:
AuthZEN Action - the operation the subject wants to perform on the resource.

Per AuthZEN 1.0 Section 5.1, `name` is REQUIRED.

name.description: REQUIRED. The name of the action.

properties.description: OPTIONAL. Additional attributes for policy evaluation.

AuthZENContext.description:
Context object for AuthZEN requests.

Must be a JSON object; non-object values are rejected.

action.description: Operation the principal wants to perform on the resource.

Optional application attributes available to policy evaluation. The
value must be a JSON object and its serialized form is bounded to
10,000 bytes.

Internal JWT claims and organization, group, and role context used by
trusted evaluation callers. HTTP handlers reject caller-supplied
values; JWT-derived context is installed only after verification.

resource.description: Resource the principal wants to access.

Internal authentication-method and assurance context used when

subject.description: Principal whose access is being evaluated.

oneOf.description:
Internal API-key identity and scope context. HTTP handlers reject
caller-supplied values on interactive routes and overwrite them with
context derived from a validated service token on runtime routes.

AuthZENEvaluationResponse.description:
AuthZEN Access Evaluation API Response.

Per AuthZEN 1.0 Section 5.2, `decision` is REQUIRED and is a boolean value.
`true` means the access is permitted, `false` means access is denied.

oneOf.description:
OPTIONAL. Step-up challenge when decision is deny due to insufficient
authentication.
OPTIONAL. Implementation-specific response context.

decision.description:
REQUIRED. Boolean indicating if access is permitted (true) or denied
(false).

while each buyer page has an explicit closed projection type. This keeps a
newly added seller field from silently crossing the buyer route boundary.

Trust state that is safe to expose to a buyer. Timeline labels and
evidence strings are intentionally omitted because they may contain
invoice, dunning-case, policy, or provider identifiers.

Customer-safe usage projection. Organization scope, reconciliation
counters, and projection diagnostics are operator evidence, while the
period and aggregate amount are useful to the customer.

ConfigureInvoiceNumberingConflictRespons.description:
The numbering configuration command has one HTTP status for two stable
conflict families: stale writers receive the authoritative current
configuration, while validation/state conflicts use the normal envelope.
Keeping the union at the route boundary makes the generated contract match
both response shapes without changing the runtime error model.

ConfigureInvoiceNumberingStableConflictR.description:
Schema-only mirror of [`http_error::ErrorEnvelope`] for this union branch.

`ErrorEnvelope` intentionally accepts future extension fields, so using it
directly in a `oneOf` would overlap the stale branch whenever a stale
payload contains `current_configuration`. The route-specific mirror keeps
the stable branch closed and therefore makes the two documented variants
disjoint without narrowing the shared error contract globally.

A `200` response is successful only when `error_code` is absent; assertion failures remain on the existing `200 OK` plus `error_code` response contract.
